# polaris_catalog (Resource)

Manage a Polaris catalog. Deletion unregisters without purging object data. Nonempty parent deletion is refused by Polaris.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "polaris_catalog" "example" {
  name                = "warehouse"
  properties          = { "default-base-location" = "file:///tmp/warehouse", "polaris.config.purge-view-metadata-on-drop" = "false" }
  storage_config_json = jsonencode({ storageType = "FILE", allowedLocations = ["file:///tmp/warehouse"] })
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Stable object name. Import existing names before applying.

### Optional

- `connection_config_json` (String, Sensitive) Experimental EXTERNAL catalog ConnectionConfigInfo. May contain credentials in state.
- `properties` (Map of String) Only these property keys are reconciled; engine-added keys are preserved.
- `storage_config_json` (String) StorageConfigInfo JSON: storageType, allowedLocations and cloud-specific fields. Does not create cloud resources.
- `type` (String) Catalog type. External federation requires server configuration.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `metadata_json` (String, Sensitive) Current object metadata, excluding response credential-vending configuration.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import polaris_catalog.example 'warehouse'
```
